skill.description: Systematic workflow for training, validating, and deploying neural networks with Flow Nexus, E2B sandboxes, Claude Flow hooks, Docker, and FastAPI.
skill.summary: Guide Flow Nexus neural network training from cluster setup through validation and deployment.
skill.author: DNYoussef

security_audit.summary: Most static detections are Markdown fences, workflow diagrams, local URLs, or illustrative labels rather than malicious code. Confirmed concerns are documented commands that may execute unpinned npx packages and a deployment example that can expose an unauthenticated inference service. No prompt injection or secret exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.suggestion: Pin Flow Nexus and Claude Flow package versions, document trusted sources, and require user confirmation before any agent runs npm commands.
Bind local examples to localhost by default, add authentication guidance, and document TLS, firewall, and reverse proxy requirements for production.
Mark generated scripts as examples, add preflight checks, and tell users to review filesystem, Docker, and network effects before execution.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Remote Package Execution
semantic_findings.description: The SOP asks users or agents to run npx flow-nexus@latest and npx claude-flow@alpha. These dist-tags can execute package code that changes over time without a pinned version.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited commands directly invoke npm packages through mutable latest and alpha tags. This is a clear supply-chain risk when automated by an agent.

semantic_findings.title: Unauthenticated Inference Service Exposure
semantic_findings.description: The deployment example binds Uvicorn to all interfaces and maps port 8000 while exposing prediction and metrics endpoints without authentication.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The service binds to 0.0.0.0 and the deploy script publishes the port. The FastAPI example shows health, predict, and metrics routes with no access control.

content.user_title: Train Neural Networks with Flow Nexus
content.value_statement: Distributed neural network training requires coordinated setup, validation, and deployment. This skill guides Flow Nexus workflows from architecture design to production serving.
actual_capabilities: Defines a phased Flow Nexus workflow for neural network setup, training, validation, and deployment.
Assigns work across machine learning, platform, and deployment specialist agents.
Provides example architecture, training, monitoring, validation, and metadata files.
Shows distributed training coordination through Flow Nexus MCP actions and Claude Flow memory hooks.
Outlines Docker and FastAPI serving steps with local health, prediction, and metrics checks.
limitations: Requires Flow Nexus MCP access and valid authentication before cloud training can run.
Uses illustrative datasets, metrics, and model identifiers that users must replace.
Includes shell, Docker, and network commands that need review before execution.
Does not replace production security, model governance, or compliance review.

use_cases.title: Plan Distributed Training
use_cases.description: Create a structured training plan with architecture, dataset, validation, and benchmark steps.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Flow Nexus Resources
use_cases.description: Map cluster setup, node deployment, memory coordination, and distributed training operations.

use_cases.title: Prepare Model Serving
use_cases.description: Draft Docker, FastAPI, health check, metrics, and deployment documentation for a trained model.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Training Run
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan a Flow Nexus neural network training run for my task, dataset type, target accuracy, and deployment goal.

prompt_templates.title: Configure the Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to propose the model architecture, hyperparameters, validation checks, and Flow Nexus resources for my neural network.

prompt_templates.title: Validate and Benchmark
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design validation tests, performance benchmarks, acceptance thresholds, and troubleshooting steps for my trained model.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Production Deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to produce a secure deployment checklist, serving API plan, monitoring plan, and rollout steps for my trained model.

output_examples.input: Train a transformer classifier with Flow Nexus and prepare it for serving.
output_examples.output: A phased plan covering authentication, cluster setup, architecture selection, distributed training, validation metrics, and deployment readiness.

output_examples.input: Review whether my trained model is ready for production.
output_examples.output: A validation summary with accuracy, latency, overfitting checks, benchmark status, and recommended deployment actions.

output_examples.input: Create a deployment handoff for a completed neural network project.
output_examples.output: A handoff outline with model metadata, serving endpoints, monitoring expectations, health checks, and operational cautions.

best_practices: Replace all placeholder model IDs, credentials, metrics, and dataset values before running commands.
Pin package versions and review shell commands before allowing an agent to execute them.
Add authentication, access controls, and observability before exposing an inference service.
anti_patterns: Running the sample deployment commands unchanged in a shared or production environment.
Treating illustrative accuracy, latency, and throughput numbers as real validation evidence.
Publishing model endpoints without authentication, rate limits, monitoring, or rollback plans.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps plan and execute a Flow Nexus neural network workflow from setup to deployment.

faq.question: Does it train a model by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow instructions and examples that require Flow Nexus tools and user-provided data.

faq.question: Which tools are referenced?
faq.answer: It references Flow Nexus MCP actions, Claude Flow hooks, E2B sandboxes, Docker, FastAPI, and TensorFlow serving concepts.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code or Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. It is written as a procedural skill for Claude, Claude Code, and Codex compatible workflows.

faq.question: What should I review before running commands?
faq.answer: Review package versions, shell scripts, Docker settings, network exposure, credentials, and local file paths.

faq.question: Is it suitable for production deployment?
faq.answer: It can support production planning, but users must add security controls, governance, testing, and operational review.
